report_md:
# NVIDIA vs. Tesla: Fiscal 2025 Revenue and Risk

## Executive Summary
- NVIDIA reported $130.5 billion in revenue, up 114%; Tesla reported $94.827 billion, down 2.93% (calculated). Their fiscal years ended more than 11 months apart, so this is not a same-period comparison. [1][2]
- NVIDIA’s growth was driven by Data Center demand; Tesla’s automotive revenue fell, partly offset by growth in energy and services. [1][2]
- Available evidence highlights NVIDIA’s direct-customer concentration and Tesla’s factory, battery-supply and international-operation risks. It does **not** support a complete or like-for-like ranking of their risks. [3][4]

## Revenue

| Fiscal 2025 | NVIDIA | Tesla |
|---|---:|---:|
| Year-end | January 26, 2025 | December 31, 2025 |
| Revenue | $130.497bn [1][5] | $94.827bn [2] |
| Year-over-year change | +114% [1] | −2.93%, calculated [2] |

**NVIDIA:** The company attributed Data Center growth to demand for Hopper accelerated computing, including for generative AI. Data Center revenue rose 142%. [1]

**Tesla:** Automotive revenue fell from $77.070 billion to $69.526 billion; energy generation and storage increased from $10.086 billion to $12.771 billion, and services and other from $10.534 billion to $12.530 billion. Tesla attributed energy growth primarily to higher Megapack and Powerwall deployments, partly offset by lower Megapack average selling prices. [2]

**Key differences:** NVIDIA’s reported revenue was $35.670 billion higher (calculated), and its growth was approximately 116.93 percentage points faster (calculated). This contrasts rapid Data Center expansion with an automotive decline partly offset by Tesla’s other revenue lines. NVIDIA’s exact revenue figure is from a secondary financial-statement compilation; its own annual report confirms the rounded $130.5 billion figure and growth rate. The periods differ substantially. [1][2][5]

## Risk

**NVIDIA:** Three direct customers accounted for 12%, 11% and 11% of fiscal 2025 sales, respectively, primarily attributable to Compute & Networking. Together that is 34% (calculated), indicating direct-customer concentration; direct customers are not necessarily the ultimate end customers. [3]

**Tesla:** Its fiscal 2025 fourth-quarter update cautioned about factory ramps, procuring battery cells—including through its own manufacturing—and international operations and expansion. These are company-identified risks in the update, not verified quotations from the December 2025 10-K risk factors. [4]

**Key differences:** The available evidence identifies concentration in NVIDIA’s direct customers versus Tesla’s operational and supply exposures. These disclosures are different kinds of evidence, not comparable measures of risk magnitude; neither establishes which company is more exposed overall. [3][4]

## Overall Comparison
NVIDIA had higher and much faster-growing reported fiscal 2025 revenue, while Tesla’s revenue declined. The risk evidence points to different exposures but is insufficient to rank them.

**Evidence gaps and uncertainty:** Researchers located both fiscal 2025 annual filings but could not retrieve substantive Item 1A risk-factor text for either company. Consequently, a complete comparison of their principal disclosed risks is unverified. The fiscal year-ends and exposure windows also differ; NVIDIA’s exact revenue amount is secondary-sourced. [1][2][5][6]

## Sources
1. [NVIDIA fiscal 2025 annual report](https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2025/annual/NVIDIA-2025-Annual-Report.pdf).
2. [Tesla fiscal 2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231.htm).
3. [NVIDIA fiscal 2025 Form 10-K](https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/177440d5-3b32-4185-8cc8-95500a9dc783.pdf).
4. [Tesla Q4 2025 update](https://assets-ir.tesla.com/tesla-contents/IR/TSLA-Q4-2025-Update.pdf).
5. [SEC API financial-statement compilation, secondary source](https://sec-api.io/media/prompts/nvidia-financial-statements/report.pdf).
6. [NVIDIA fiscal 2025 Form 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581025000023/nvda-20250126.htm).

notes.nvidia-tesla-fy2025-revenue-drivers.md:
## Research Question
What were NVIDIA’s and Tesla’s fiscal 2025 revenues, year-over-year growth, principal revenue drivers and fiscal year-end dates?

## Key Findings
- [Fact] NVIDIA’s fiscal year ended **January 26, 2025**; revenue was **$130.497 billion**, up **114%** year over year. Its annual report attributes Data Center growth to demand for Hopper accelerated computing for large language models, recommendation engines and generative AI. Data Center revenue grew 142% year over year. [NVIDIA annual report](https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2025/annual/NVIDIA-2025-Annual-Report.pdf); [secondary financial-statement compilation](https://sec-api.io/media/prompts/nvidia-financial-statements/report.pdf).
- [Fact] Tesla’s fiscal year ended **December 31, 2025**; revenue was **$94.827 billion**, down **2.93% calculated** from 2024. Automotive revenue was its largest revenue line, but fell; increased energy and services revenue partly offset the decline. Tesla attributed energy growth primarily to increased Megapack and Powerwall deployments, partly offset by lower Megapack average selling prices. [Tesla 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231.htm).
- [Interpretation] NVIDIA’s revenue exceeded Tesla’s by **$35.670 billion**, calculated, but the fiscal years ended more than 11 months apart and cover different 12-month periods.

## Financial Facts
- **NVIDIA:** FY2025 total revenue **$130.497 billion**, versus FY2024 **$60.922 billion**; Data Center FY2025 **$115.186 billion**, versus **$47.525 billion**. Exact amounts from a [secondary financial-statement compilation](https://sec-api.io/media/prompts/nvidia-financial-statements/report.pdf); the [company annual report](https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2025/annual/NVIDIA-2025-Annual-Report.pdf) reports rounded total revenue of $130.5 billion and 114% growth.
- **Tesla:** FY2025 total revenue **$94.827 billion**, versus FY2024 **$97.690 billion**. FY2025 automotive revenue was **$69.526 billion**, versus **$77.070 billion**; energy generation and storage **$12.771 billion**, versus **$10.086 billion**; services and other **$12.530 billion**, versus **$10.534 billion**. [Company 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231.htm).

## Sources
- NVIDIA, FY2025 annual report: https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2025/annual/NVIDIA-2025-Annual-Report.pdf
- NVIDIA, FY2025 fourth-quarter and full-year earnings release: https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025
- Tesla, FY2025 Form 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231.htm
- SEC API, secondary financial-statement compilation: https://sec-api.io/media/prompts/nvidia-financial-statements/report.pdf

## Caveats
Fiscal year-ends differ substantially; these are each company’s FY2025, not aligned calendar periods or their latest reported years. NVIDIA’s exact revenue and Data Center figures are from a secondary compilation: the retrieved company report excerpt confirmed only rounded total revenue and growth. Tesla’s percentage decline and the revenue difference are calculated from the cited figures. Tesla’s automotive revenue line excludes services and other, unlike its broader automotive segment total.

## Research Question
Which substantive principal risks did NVIDIA and Tesla disclose in their respective fiscal 2025 10-Ks, and what company-specific evidence supports comparison?

## Key Findings
- [Fact] Both historical 10-Ks were located, but the retrieved extracts did **not** expose substantive Item 1A risk text. Tesla’s filing index places Item 1A on pages 12–27. The specific risks in those sections therefore remain unverified from the retrieved evidence. [NVIDIA](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581025000023/nvda-20250126.htm); [Tesla](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231.htm).
- [Fact] Tesla’s fiscal-2025 Q4 update provides alternative company evidence of risks concerning factory ramps, procuring battery cells—including through its own manufacturing—and international operations and expansion. Its cautionary language references the 10-K filed January 30, 2025 and subsequent 10-Qs; these points are **not verified as Item 1A disclosures in Tesla’s December 2025 10-K**. [Tesla Q4 update](https://assets-ir.tesla.com/tesla-contents/IR/TSLA-Q4-2025-Update.pdf).
- [Fact] Tesla’s FY2025 10-K says it entered autonomous ride-hailing with a Robotaxi launch in June 2025. This establishes company-specific operating context, but the retrieved passage does not identify a corresponding Item 1A risk. [Tesla 10-K](https://ir.tesla.com/_flysystem/s3/sec/000162828026003952/tsla-20251231-gen.pdf).
- [Interpretation] A substantive like-for-like risk comparison is not supportable from these extracts: NVIDIA-specific FY2025 risk details and Tesla’s December 2025 Item 1A wording remain unverified.
